 1          WHEREAS, the above-captioned Related Cases currently are pending in this District and
 2 concern substantially the same parties, property, transaction, or event;

 3          WHEREAS, the above-captioned matter, McPhee v. Prosper Funding, LLC, was the first-
 4   filed and is the furthest along, procedurally, among the Related Cases;
 5          WHEREAS, the Parties agree that this Stipulation is being entered into without waiving
 6   any party’s rights or ability to raise any defenses or claims (including jurisdictional challenges)
 7   and expressly reserve all rights regarding the same;
 8          WHEREAS, the Parties agree that the Related Cases should be consolidated for pre-trial
 9   purposes in the interests of efficiency and judicial economy, and to avoid unnecessary duplication
10   of effort and resources. Accordingly, all counsel for the Parties to the Related Cases jointly
11   stipulate and request that the Court enter an Order consolidating the Related Cases for pre-trial
12   purposes and permitting the filing of a single Consolidated Class Action Complaint; and
13          WHEREAS, the Parties agree that it would be duplicative and wasteful of the Court’s and
14   the Parties’ resources for Defendants to be required to separately respond to the complaints in the
15   Related Actions prior to the filing of a Consolidated Class Action Complaint, should the Court
16   order the requested consolidation;
17          NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS STIPULATED AND AGREED, and the Parties request,
18   that the Court order the following:
19          1.      The Related Cases are consolidated for all pre-trial purposes (the “Consolidated
20   Action”) pursuant to Fed. R. Civ. P. 42(a).

22   Action” will bear Lead Case 3:25-cv-07947-CRB, the number assigned to the first-filed case and

 1 including Plaintiff and Class Members, were required to entrust Defendant with highly sensitive PII,

            Access to the system is tightly controlled and limited to only those who have a need

     expectation and mutual understanding that Defendant would comply with its promises and obligations

     to keep such information confidential and protected against unauthorized access.

                      COMPLAINT FOR DAMAGES, INJUNCTIVE AND EQUITABLE RELIEF
                                            CASE NO.

 1          31.     Plaintiff and Class Members value the confidentiality of their PII and demand security

 2 to safeguard their PII. To that end, Plaintiff and Class Members have taken reasonable steps to

     maintain the confidentiality of their PII.

            32.     Defendant derived economic benefits from collecting Plaintiff’s and Class Members’

     PII. Without the required submission of PII, Defendant could not perform its lending operations or

 7 generate revenue.

            34.     Defendant had and has a duty to adopt reasonable measures to keep Plaintiff’s and

 8

            39.     Cyberattacks have become so notorious that the FBI and U.S. Secret Service have

            41.     Cyber-attacks against financial institutions such as Defendant are targeted and

23
            43.     The Federal Trade Commission (“FTC”) has promulgated numerous guides for
24
     businesses which highlight the importance of implementing reasonable data security practices.
25
     According to the FTC, the need for data security should be factored into all business decision-making.

            44.     In 2016, the FTC updated its publication, Protecting Personal Information: A Guide

28 for Business, which established cyber-security guidelines for businesses. The guidelines note that
                                                -8-

 1 businesses should protect the personal customer information that they keep; properly dispose of

     monitor for suspicious activity on the network; and verify that third-party service providers have

 9          51.     The GLBA states, “It is the policy of the Congress that each financial institution has

26

27
     numerous rules and regulations promulgated under the GLBA.
28

                                            CASE NO.
         Case 3:25-cv-08169-CRB          Document 1       Filed 09/25/25      Page 11 of 37




 1          56.     The Safeguards Rule, which implements Section 501(b) of the GLBA, 15 U.S.C. §
